note: Task #150 — per-CHAMPION render-size overrides. As of #150 ChampionView HEIGHT-NORMALIZES every loaded champion glb to a common target height (render/views/ChampionView.ts TARGET_HEIGHT ≈ 1.8u) instead of applying each model doc's raw `scale` as an absolute — so by DEFAULT every champion reads the same on-screen size regardless of its glb's wildly-varying native mesh height (the #61 audit only checked the 2.5u ceiling, never relative consistency; measured spread was 1.70u..2.32u, with the four shared CC0 stand-in meshes — champ.sela renders 2.32u — the oversized group, and 夏娜/imported.heroshana at 1.70u reading small next to them). `relativeScale` is the per-champion RELATIVE multiplier on top of that normalization (1.0 = the normalized target height; <1 = deliberately smaller, >1 = bigger) — the ONLY knob for INTENTIONAL size exceptions (lore-small creatures/mascots, lore-large giants/mecha). Absent champions default to 1.0 (normal human = 夏娜). Keyed by championId. The optional `glbPath`/`clipMap` still swap in a genuinely different model (task #77). Files under content/models beginning with _ are NOT model@1 docs (like _index.json) and are skipped by the content validators/index builder. The composition root (GameApp) loads this map and feeds EntityViewRegistry.modelOverrideFor -> applyModelOverride (`relativeScale` threads to ChampionView.tryUpgradeToGlb); wiring that championId->override lookup in GameApp is the remaining composition-root step (owned by the GameApp wave, see docs/todo/models.md mdl-64). Height-normalization itself needs NO wiring and is live for every champion. Legacy note: pre-#150 this field was `scale` (an ABSOLUTE render scale, e.g. 小叮噹 0.6); it is now `relativeScale` with the new meaning. See docs/_model-size-audit-150.md.
